investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes are excluded by node affinity or selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod creation attempt times out as Unschedulable before a VM is assigned, preventing the eval from collecting any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, artificially limiting the schedulable pool. The 4 excluded nodes could otherwise provide capacity. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — Cluster-wide node count is too small for the expected remote agent concurrency: with only 6 nodes total and 4 excluded by affinity, the effective scheduling pool is 2 nodes, which may be undersized for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads. Supported by the cluster topology implied in failed-check.message.

LOW PROBABILITY — Transient spike in remote agent demand at the time of the eval run (2026-06-19T10:57–11:05Z) temporarily exhausted VM slots that would otherwise be available. Cannot be confirmed or ruled out without cluster utilization metrics at that timestamp.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T11:00–11:05Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agents workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. With only 2 eligible nodes and both reporting "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled. Preemption is also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent creation step, so no evidence is produced and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, confirming the failure occurred at the infrastructure scheduling layer before any agent runtime code could execute.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place remote agent pods on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource had no remaining allocatable capacity, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because pod scheduling failed, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, no agent was created, and the eval produced zero evidence — leaving all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) missing. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure-layer constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes are excluded by node affinity or selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod creation attempt times out as Unschedulable before a VM is assigned, preventing the eval from collecting any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, artificially limiting the schedulable pool. The 4 excluded nodes could otherwise provide capacity. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — Cluster-wide node count is too small for the expected remote agent concurrency: with only 6 nodes total and 4 excluded by affinity, the effective scheduling pool is 2 nodes, which may be undersized for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads. Supported by the cluster topology implied in failed-check.message.

LOW PROBABILITY — Transient spike in remote agent demand at the time of the eval run (2026-06-19T10:57–11:05Z) temporarily exhausted VM slots that would otherwise be available. Cannot be confirmed or ruled out without cluster utilization metrics at that timestamp.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, confirming the failure occurred at the infrastructure scheduling layer before any agent runtime code could execute.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place remote agent pods on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource had no remaining allocatable capacity, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because pod scheduling failed, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, no agent was created, and the eval produced zero evidence — leaving all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) missing. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure-layer constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the extended resource pool for peer-pod VMs is fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. All three sibling checks report the same scheduler message, making this the strongest candidate (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules recently became more restrictive, or if nodes were cordoned or relabeled, the effective schedulable pool would shrink and exhaust faster.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agent workload: the total number of nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 of 6) may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus any live workload sharing the same resource, causing contention.

Low probability — transient spike in concurrent remote agent creation: if multiple eval runs or user-initiated agents were scheduled simultaneously, the 2 eligible nodes could be temporarily saturated even if baseline capacity is normally sufficient.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes shows available (non-zero) allocatable capacity at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If a subsequent eval run with identical configuration succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload briefly exhausted capacity) rather than a sustained resource shortage.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector rules are found to be intentionally restrictive and unchanged, and the 2 eligible nodes have never had sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity for concurrent runs, the root cause is cluster under-provisioning rather than exhaustion from a new workload.

If the 4 excluded nodes are found to have been recently relabeled or cordoned (reducing the eligible pool from a previously larger set), the root cause would be node configuration drift rather than resource exhaustion on the 2 remaining nodes.
